data.q: What is the correct signature for a benchmark function in Go's testing package?
data.e: Benchmark functions must start with 'Benchmark' and accept a pointer to testing.B. The testing.B type provides methods like RunParallel, ResetTimer, and N for iteration control.

data.q: Which command runs all benchmarks in a package and reports memory allocation statistics?
data.e: The flag -bench=. matches all benchmarks. -benchmem enables memory allocation statistics (allocs/op, bytes/op) in the output.

data.q: In a benchmark function, what does b.N represent?
o: The number of CPU cores available
The number of times the benchmark loop should run
The number of bytes allocated per operation
The number of goroutines to spawn
data.e: b.N is set by the testing framework and indicates how many iterations the benchmark loop must execute. The framework increases N until the benchmark runs long enough for a stable measurement.

data.q: How do you run a specific subtest named 'CaseA' inside a test function 'TestFoo' from the command line?
data.e: The -run flag takes a regex matching the full test path. Subtests are separated by a slash. 'TestFoo/CaseA' matches the subtest CaseA inside TestFoo.

data.q: Which method on testing.T marks the current test as failed but continues execution?
data.e: t.Error() logs the error and marks the test as failed but continues execution. t.Fatal() and t.FailNow() stop the test immediately (via runtime.Goexit). t.Fail() marks failed but logs nothing.

data.q: What is the purpose of t.Helper() in a test helper function?
o: It marks the function as a test helper so file/line numbers in errors point to the caller
It runs the helper function in a separate goroutine
It automatically calls t.Fail() if the helper returns an error
It registers the helper for cleanup after the test
data.e: t.Helper() marks the calling function as a test helper. When the helper calls t.Error/Fatal, the reported file/line number will be the call site in the test function, not inside the helper.

data.q: Which flag enables the race detector during testing?
data.e: The -race flag instruments the code to detect data races at runtime. It is supported on linux/amd64, freebsd/amd64, darwin/amd64, windows/amd64.

data.q: How do you benchmark a function that runs in parallel using testing.B?
o: b.SetParallelism(true); for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ { ... }
b.Parallel(func() { for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ { ... } })
data.e: b.RunParallel creates multiple goroutines and distributes b.N iterations among them. The closure receives a *testing.PB; pb.Next() returns true until the goroutine's share of iterations is exhausted.

data.q: What does b.ResetTimer() do in a benchmark?
o: Resets the benchmark iteration count (b.N) to zero
Zeros the elapsed time and memory allocation counters, excluding setup code from measurements
Restarts the benchmark from the beginning with a new b.N
Resets the system clock for the benchmark process
data.e: b.ResetTimer() zeros the elapsed time and memory allocation metrics. It is typically called after expensive setup code so only the target operation is measured.

data.q: Which function runs once before all tests in a package for setup, and once after for teardown?
data.e: TestMain(m *testing.M) is the entry point for package-level setup/teardown. Call m.Run() to execute the tests. Return value of m.Run() should be passed to os.Exit.

data.q: What is the effect of calling t.Parallel() in a test function?
o: Runs the test function concurrently with other tests marked Parallel
Runs the test function in a separate process
Splits the test function into multiple goroutines automatically
Enables parallel execution of subtests only
data.e: t.Parallel() signals that this test can run in parallel with other tests that also call t.Parallel(). The test will pause until all non-parallel tests complete, then run concurrently with other parallel tests.

data.q: How do you measure throughput (bytes processed per second) in a benchmark?
o: b.SetBytes(n) where n is the number of bytes processed per iteration
data.e: b.SetBytes(n) records the number of bytes processed in each iteration. The framework then reports throughput in MB/s (or GB/s) alongside ns/op.

data.q: Which method creates a temporary directory that is automatically cleaned up when the test finishes?
data.e: t.TempDir() (added in Go 1.15) returns a path to a new temporary directory. It registers a cleanup function via t.Cleanup to remove the directory when the test and all its subtests complete.

data.q: What is the purpose of the -count flag in 'go test'?
o: Specifies the number of CPU cores to use
Runs the tests/benchmarks N times (useful for flaky tests or benchmark stability)
Limits the number of test functions executed
Sets the number of iterations for benchmarks (overrides b.N)
data.e: -count=N runs the test suite N times. For benchmarks, it runs each benchmark N times, reporting each result separately. Useful for detecting flaky tests or observing benchmark variance.

data.q: How do you skip a test conditionally (e.g., short mode) in Go?
o: if testing.Short() { t.Skip("skipping in short mode") }
data.e: testing.Short() returns true when -test.short flag is set. t.Skip() marks the test as skipped (not failed) and stops execution via runtime.Goexit. t.SkipNow() is the low-level equivalent but t.Skip() allows a message.

data.q: Which interface do both *testing.T and *testing.B implement, allowing shared helper functions?
data.e: testing.TB is the common interface implemented by *testing.T, *testing.B, and *testing.F (fuzzing). It includes methods like Error, Fatal, Log, Helper, Cleanup, TempDir, Context.

data.q: What does the -cover flag do when running 'go test'?
o: Runs tests with code coverage analysis and prints a summary
Covers all test files in the module
Generates an HTML coverage report automatically
data.e: -cover enables coverage analysis. It instruments the code to track which statements are executed during tests and prints a summary (e.g., 'coverage: 85.2% of statements'). Use -coverprofile=out to save details.

data.q: In a fuzz test (Go 1.18+), what is the correct signature for the fuzz target function?
data.e: Fuzz tests start with 'Fuzz' and accept *testing.F. The *testing.F type provides methods like Add (for seed corpus) and Fuzz (for the fuzzing function).

data.q: How do you run only benchmarks matching a specific pattern, e.g., 'BenchmarkSort'?
data.e: -bench takes a regular expression to match benchmark names. -run matches test functions. The regex 'BenchmarkSort' matches any benchmark with that substring.

data.q: What is the correct way to stop the timer temporarily during a benchmark to exclude expensive setup?
data.e: b.StopTimer() pauses the timer; b.StartTimer() resumes it. This excludes the setup code duration from the benchmark measurement. ResetTimer zeros the counters entirely.

data.q: Which method registers a function to be called when the test (and its subtests) completes?
data.e: t.Cleanup(f) registers f to be called after the test and all its subtests finish. Cleanups run in LIFO order. It is the modern replacement for defer in tests, works correctly with t.Parallel and subtests.
